They need a site that shows the work, explains the process, and makes it easy for the right client to reach out. Kodely builds that from a plain-English description and puts it live on a real URL the same session, with no design software and no code required.

What an interior designer website actually needs

Strip away the trends and every interior design site that converts is doing the same handful of jobs well:

  • A strong project portfolio that lets the work speak first, organized by room type, style, or project scale.
  • A clear design philosophy so a visitor knows in ten seconds whether your aesthetic fits their taste.
  • Services and process that demystify what working with a designer actually involves, from first call to final install.
  • Client testimonials that build the trust a purely visual portfolio cannot.
  • A low-friction way to start a conversation, usually a consultation inquiry form rather than a hard sales pitch.

Must-have sections

SectionWhy it matters
Home / heroSets the aesthetic immediately with a signature project image and a one-line positioning statement.
Portfolio / projectsThe core of the site. Grouped galleries beat a single long scroll.
About / philosophyYour design point of view, background, and what makes your studio different.
Services / processWhat you offer and what it is like to work together, step by step.
TestimonialsShort, specific client quotes tied to real projects build credibility fast.
Consultation / contactA simple form that asks for the details you actually need to qualify a lead.

A real example prompt

You do not need a spec document. A few sentences of context is enough for Kodely to generate a complete first draft. Here is a prompt that works well for a design studio:

Example prompt: Build a portfolio website for my interior design studio, Marlowe & Co. We focus on warm minimalist residential interiors: kitchens, living rooms, and primary suites. I want a hero section with a bold statement, a project gallery organized into three categories, an about section describing our design philosophy, a services section covering full-service design and design-only consulting, a testimonials section, and a consultation request form asking for name, email, project type, and budget range. Use a warm neutral palette, off-white background, and elegant serif headings.

Kodely reads that and generates a real Vite plus React 19 app in TypeScript with Tailwind CSS v4, not a page builder template with your text dropped in. The layout, components, and copy are all generated together, built from a real foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives, so the result looks like a designed site rather than a form response.

What Kodely generates, honestly

Kodely produces a genuine multi-section portfolio site: a hero, categorized project galleries, a philosophy or about section, a services and process breakdown, a testimonials block, and a consultation inquiry form UI. It does this well and it does it fast. Here is what it does not do yet, and you should know this going in: the project galleries ship with placeholder visuals that you swap for your own real photography after the site is built, and the consultation form is a real, styled UI component, not a connected booking or payment system. Kodely does not generate backends, databases, authentication, or payment processing. If a prospective client submits that form today, you will need to wire it to whatever inbox or CRM tool you already use. What you get is a professional, real-code foundation you can extend, not a black-box mockup.

Customizing your site

Every change happens the same way it started: describe it in chat. Ask for a different hero layout, a fourth project category, a warmer color palette, or a rewritten philosophy paragraph, and Kodely edits the actual component files rather than layering a patch on top. The live preview updates as it builds so you see the real compiled app, not a static rendering. If a change goes somewhere you did not want, every successful generation is a checkpoint, and rolling back to a previous version is free. If you want to see exactly what changed under the hood, the code view shows you the actual generated source files in the app.

Publishing live

When the site looks right, Publish puts it live on a real public address at yourstudioname.kodely.site, included at no extra cost with no separate hosting step to configure. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you are not shipping a mistake along with your portfolio. There are no custom domains yet, only the kodely.site subdomain, and there is no code export or zip download today, only in-app viewing and copying of your source files.

FAQ

Do I need any design or coding experience?

No. You describe the site you want in plain English and Kodely generates the real components. Editing later works the same way.

Will the portfolio use my actual project photos?

Kodely generates the gallery structure and layout with placeholder visuals first. You add your real photography afterward; there is no automated photo hosting or upload pipeline built in yet.

Can clients actually book a consultation through the form?

The consultation section is a real, styled form component, not a connected booking or payment system. You will need to connect it to your own inbox, calendar, or CRM.

What does it cost to get started?

Every new account gets 750 free credits with no credit card required, enough to generate and publish a full site. If you need more, top-ups start at nine dollars for 500 credits, and a build that fails to compile is never charged.

Can I use my own domain name?

Not yet. Every published site currently lives at a free yourname.kodely.site address.

Ready to see your studio online? Build your interior design site free and have a live draft before your next client call.
